text: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. We live in an age of unprecedented access to information. But figuring out what to trust is becoming increasingly difficult. Social media algorithms shape what we see, headlines compete for our attention, and generative AI can now create remarkably convincing images, videos, and other content. In this interactive workshop, participants will build practical media and AI literacy skills for navigating this changing landscape. The workshop aims to help participants become critical thinkers and confident consumers of information and AI. About the Speaker: Tracy Wu is the founder of Meiflower, a Los Altos-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit focused on helping children, families, and communities develop the critical-thinking and digital-literacy skills needed to thrive in an increasingly technology-filled world. Tracy brings decades of corporate experience and a master's degree in finance. Most recently, she served as a Senior Program Manager in Platform Trust & Safety at LinkedIn, with experience related to online safety, platform integrity, and user trust. In the community, Tracy is also an Art Docent with the Los Altos School District and a reading tutor through the Santa Clara County Library District's Adult Literacy Program. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
